findings.title: Auto-find and execute script one-liner
findings.description: The documentation instructs finding and executing a script via a shell one-liner. While this does not fetch remote content (local file execution only), it encourages blind script execution patterns. The script itself is local, so this is low risk, but the pattern of auto-discovering and executing scripts could be leveraged if an attacker plants a malicious main.py in the skills path.
findings.recommendation: Pin the script to an explicit, verified path rather than using a wildcard `find` that could match an attacker-planted file. E.g., `python3.10 skills/llm-gateway/scripts/main.py list_models --key-type personal` with a checksum verification step.
findings.span: SCRIPT=$(find skills -name "main.py" -path "*llm-gateway*" 2>/dev/null | head -1) && python3.10 "$SCRIPT" list_models --key-type personal

findings.title: Skill documentation directs AI to auto-execute scripts
findings.description: The SKILL.md contains directive language instructing the AI assistant to execute scripts automatically rather than showing code for review. This is characteristic of skill files (which legitimately direct agent behavior), but the emphatic 'EXECUTE the script and return real results' instructions reduce the user's opportunity to review actions before they run against a live gateway with credentials.
findings.recommendation: Add a confirmation gate before executing scripts that use credentials (AMD_LLM_API_KEY), and ensure the agent surfaces the exact command to the user before running it. Frame execution as a suggestion requiring user consent rather than a mandate.
findings.span: **IMPORTANT: For list/validate/troubleshoot requests, EXECUTE the script and return real results. Do NOT just show code.**

findings.title: Unused internal registry endpoint defined
findings.description: A REGISTRY_URL constant pointing to an internal host (atlvcpdmapp02) is defined but not used anywhere in the script. Dead configuration referencing internal infrastructure can hint at future scope expansion or leftover code from a broader tool, and exposes an internal hostname in distributed code.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused REGISTRY_URL and SKILL_ASSET_ID constants if not used, or document and gate their usage. Avoid embedding internal hostnames in code distributed to client projects.

findings.title: Gateway error bodies returned to output
findings.description: Raw gateway HTTP error bodies (truncated to 500 chars) are returned in the JSON output. Although the API key is redacted via _redact_secret, other internal gateway details (deployment names, internal Azure resource identifiers) could be disclosed. The code even acknowledges internal resource names like 'pdue-aoai-...' and 'dvue-aoai-001-gpt-5-codex' may appear.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize error bodies further before surfacing, stripping known internal resource-name patterns (e.g., `*-aoai-*`) in addition to the API key, or return a generic error message with details only under an explicit debug flag.
